lamps.name: Tolomeo Mini
features: Won the Compasso d’Oro in 1989
Balanced arm that is easy to reposition
One of the most copied desk lamps ever made
lamps.story: De Lucchi, a leading Italian designer and Memphis member, co-designed it with Fassina. Several Tolomeos once sat on the desks of Apple's Industrial Design studio. Fatih uses his on his work desk, attached to a USM Haller table with an adaptor he designed himself.

lamps.name: Tizio Micro
features: No wires along the arms: the arms carry the current
Counterweights let you move it with one finger
Smaller version of the original Tizio
lamps.story: Sapper, who later designed the first IBM ThinkPad and Alessi's 9090 espresso maker, made the Tizio because he wanted a better lamp for his own desk. “Tizio” is Italian for “dude”. The small red details are his signature, like the red TrackPoint on the ThinkPad.

lamps.name: Akari 1A
features: Washi paper shade gives a gentle, warm glow
One of the earliest and simplest Akari shapes
Light, sculptural form
lamps.story: Noguchi started the Akari series in 1951 after visiting Gifu, a city known for paper lanterns. “Akari” means light in Japanese, both as illumination and lightness. Fatih bought this one secondhand in Germany and a friend brought it to him.

lamps.name: Akari 3A
features: 56 cm tall, with longer legs than the 1A
Wooden trim at top and bottom
Best on a low table, sideboard or cabinet
lamps.story: A taller sibling of the 1A. Its size is a little awkward: too short for the floor and a bit too big for a normal desk, so it lives on low furniture.

lamps.name: Akari 16A
features: Distinctive shape that still almost disappears into the room
Handmade at Ozeki in Gifu with traditional methods
lamps.story: The first Akari Fatih bought. It started in his office and later moved to the bedroom. Every Akari is still made by hand at Ozeki, the family-run workshop Noguchi worked with.

lamps.name: Akari 75A
features: Roughly 75 cm across, the biggest lamp in the house
Red sun-and-moon stamp marks an authentic Akari
lamps.story: It replaced the 16A in the office and gives the room real presence. Noguchi designed more than 100 Akari models in his lifetime.

lamps.name: PH 5
features: Bulb is never directly visible, so the light stays soft
50 cm shade gives it the “5”
Small red and blue inner parts warm the light
lamps.story: Fatih first noticed it hanging over the dinner table in the Danish film Another Round, then saw one in Dieter Rams’ house. It is one of the most famous Danish lamps and very common in Danish homes.

lamps.name: PH 3/2
features: First lamp to use Henningsen's three-shade system
Mouth-blown glass, shiny outside and matte inside
Gold medal at the 1925 Paris exhibition
lamps.story: The three-shade idea came more than 30 years before the PH 5. The glass is fragile: Fatih broke it by accident and waited months for a replacement.

lamps.name: AJ Wall Lamp
features: Tilting head: aim at the wall for indirect light or at a book for reading
Designed for the SAS Royal Hotel in Copenhagen
lamps.story: Jacobsen designed almost everything for the SAS Royal Hotel, down to the cutlery, which later appeared in 2001: A Space Odyssey.

lamps.name: Lampe de Bureau
features: Made from a single bent sheet of steel
Engineered, almost brutal look
Available from Vitra in its original colors
lamps.story: Prouvé, a French designer and metalworker best known for the Standard Chair, designed it for student residences in Nancy.

lamps.name: Chispa
features: Rechargeable and water resistant
Three light levels
Metal cage inspired by old garage lamps
lamps.story: “Chispa” means spark in Spanish. Fatih carries it around the house and uses it in the garden in summer.

lamps.name: Lamp 01
features: Real glass blocks from 1970s–80s Soviet-era buildings
Film and theater filters change the light color
lamps.story: Kismas is a small studio in Vilnius; the name means change or transformation in Lithuanian. Fatih finds it very artistic but not very functional, and swapping the filters is cumbersome.

lamps.name: Tokio Lamp
features: Shade shaped like a mailbox
Originally made by Stilnovo, reissued in 2020
lamps.story: Fatih spotted it through a shop window in Copenhagen. It was out of stock, so he later had it shipped to Germany and brought it from there to Ankara.

lamps.name: Vision 20/20 Floor
features: Two lights, one up and one down, each with its own dimmer
Base slides under a sofa
Made for reading
lamps.story: Named after the optician's eye test. It sits next to Fatih's Eames chair and comes on whenever he settles into a book.

lamps.name: Apex Floor Lamp
features: Shade is one folded sheet of steel
Shade rotates 360° for indirect light off a wall
Inspired by the classic banker's lamp
lamps.story: Fatih chose the black version for the floor lamp.

lamps.name: Apex Clip Lamp
features: Same folded steel shade, in green
Clip mount instead of a stand
lamps.story: The stock clip was ugly and hard to mount on Vitsoe 606 e-tracks, so Fatih designed a 3D-printed attachment; it took a few iterations to get right.

lamps.name: Block Lamp
features: Single 3D-printed piece, no glue or bolts
Front handle can be pulled, pushed or rotated
Can be placed three different ways
lamps.story: Fatih's own design, made in January 2025 for the shelves of his espresso bar. Ideas for the future include a battery for portability and a CNC-milled or wooden housing.
